# Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)

Vendor-neutral guidance. Model providers, vector stores, and frameworks are implementation choices recorded in docs/engineering/PROJECT.md.

## Ingestion and indexing

- Keep ingestion as a separate, re-runnable pipeline: load -> clean -> chunk -> embed -> index. Each stage is independently testable.
- Preserve source metadata on every chunk: document id, title, location (page, section, URL), version or timestamp, and access-control attributes.
- Choose chunk boundaries that follow document structure (headings, paragraphs) over fixed character counts; record the chunking parameters with the index.
- Version the index. Record the embedding model and chunking configuration it was built with; never mix embeddings from different models in one index.
- Ingestion is idempotent: re-ingesting a document replaces its chunks instead of duplicating them.

## Retrieval

- Retrieval is a function with a typed contract: query in, ranked list of chunks with scores and metadata out. Keep it independent of generation so it can be evaluated alone.
- Apply access control at retrieval time: filter by the caller's permissions before ranking, never after generation.
- Consider hybrid retrieval (lexical plus semantic) and a re-ranking step when evaluation shows recall or precision problems; add them because of measured results, not by default.
- Apply a relevance threshold. Returning nothing is better than returning irrelevant context.

## Context assembly

- Assemble context deterministically: ordered by relevance, deduplicated, and within an explicit token budget reserved for evidence.
- Delimit each retrieved passage clearly and label it with its source identifier so the model can cite it.
- Treat retrieved content as data, not instructions. Instruct the model to ignore instructions found inside passages, and never let retrieved text select tools or change system behavior.

## Grounding and insufficient evidence

- The prompt instructs the model to answer only from the provided passages.
- Define explicit behavior when evidence is insufficient or contradictory: say what is missing, and do not fill gaps from general knowledge unless the product explicitly allows it and labels it.
- Detect the empty-retrieval case in code and short-circuit to the insufficient-evidence response rather than calling the model with no evidence.

## Source attribution

- Every answer lists the sources it relied on, using identifiers that map back to the retrieved chunks.
- Validate citations in code: each cited identifier must exist in the context that was provided. Drop or flag answers with fabricated citations.
- Show users enough source detail (title, location, link) to verify the claim.

## Observability

- Log, per request: query, retrieved chunk ids and scores, index version, prompt template version, and model identifier. Apply the privacy baseline to query text.
- Version prompt templates alongside code.

## Testing

- Unit-test chunking, metadata propagation, context assembly, budget enforcement, and citation validation deterministically, without a model.
- Use a small fixed corpus in tests. Stub the model in unit tests; exercise the real model only in evaluation runs.
- Retrieval and answer quality are measured with the retrieval-evaluation workflow, not with unit-test assertions on model output.
